negative_reviews.author: kristina barkauskyte
negative_reviews.text:
Lovely Food, but Disappointing Customer Service

Today, we visited Maki & Ramen with friends. This wasn’t our first visit, and there’s a reason we decided to come back! The food was absolutely lovely, as always, and the atmosphere was really nice too. Unfortunately, our experience took a disappointing turn when it came time to pay.

When we approached the till and asked about our bill, the gentleman serving us already seemed visibly unhappy and irritated. However, things got even worse when we politely asked if we could pay separately. His reaction was completely unnecessary. He threw the card machine aside and looked at us as though we had asked for our food for free!

We were honestly shocked by his attitude. Asking to split a bill is a perfectly normal request, and no customer should be made to feel uncomfortable or unwelcome for simply asking.

Thankfully, another gentleman came over, and he was the complete opposite — very friendly, polite and happy to help us with exactly what we had asked for. We really appreciated his kindness and professionalism.

Unfortunately, despite the delicious food and lovely atmosphere, the behaviour of the first staff member left a very unpleasant feeling and spoiled what had otherwise been a great visit.

We genuinely enjoy coming to Maki & Ramen, which makes this experience even more disappointing. Good food brings customers in, but good customer service is what makes them want to return.

Hopefully, this is something management will take seriously, as no customer deserves to be treated that way.

negative_reviews.author: James Callander
negative_reviews.text: More like a chain than a premium restaurant.Noodles had a weird consistency and only a few pieces of chicken with a bucketful of noodles. Received meals at different times. Staff were attentive even though busy. The flavours of my broth were alright but too many noodles. Underwhelming.

issues: Sales and covers down year on year, but target beaten by roughly 1,500 to 3,000 GBP with 5,500 GBP of discounts.
Deliveroo orders down; inaccurate orders up to 93 because chicken katsu cutlets were packed in the smaller yellow boxes.
Duplicate numbers for sushi, sides and drinks for consecutive weeks.
Food variance 1.2%, drinks 1.0%.
A 2 star and a 1 star review, the latter suspected AI generated after a bill splitting dispute.
Roit hired FOH with a view to supervisor; Rahit onboarding; Elliot getting FOH training.
Compliance 95%; a van is needed to clear the back room clutter.
Region: food spend target temporarily raised to 26% until current promotions end (Matthew Jenner).
Region: hats or hairnets mandatory for all staff to prevent food contamination.
Region: menu to be redesigned with spice levels built into all ramen dishes and free chillies removed.
Region: GM and HC meeting notes must run through Google Meet so Gemini takes the notes; budget router templates updated, Monday dates must be entered correctly.
Year on year, covers fell by 703 (29.82%) to 1,654 and spend per head by £3.11 (12.44%) to £21.89.
Week on week, covers rose by 193 (11%) and spend per head by £0.18, but the £23 SPH target was missed.
Sales were £45,225.84, up £1,680.37 week on week and £3,225.84 (7.68%) above the target, which was raised to £42,000 this week.
Steak Tataki (265), Chicken Yakisoba (223) and Chicken Gyoza (212) were the top sellers, while octopus sashimi sold once and scallop and clam nigiri did not sell.
Drinks (12.78%) and sides (16.03%) rose while sushi slipped slightly to 17.04%, against targets of 10%, 20% and 13.5%.

Operational labour was 20.13% (£9,184.70) and total labour 23.8% (£10,766.36) against a 22% target, with 624.33 hours used and a FOH and BOH split of 43.7% and 56.3% against a 45% and 55% target; FOH and BOH agreed shift changes for next week to rebalance.
The budget rota is complete for the week commencing 12 October and drafted for the week commencing 19 October.
Food cost was 23.08% against the 25% target, down from 24.26% last week.
84% of reviews were 4 or 5 star against the 95% target, with ten 5 star, one 3 star and one 2 star.
The 3 star review praised the food but said the cashier was irritated when asked to split the bill; the GM/HC notes say the customer was difficult and the manager on shift dealt with it properly.

The 2 star review complained about noodle consistency and portions (too many noodles and few pieces of chicken), meals arriving at different times and the restaurant being a chain rather than premium.
Aberdeen was not on the 13/10 Scotland BOH call.
Elliot is being trained up for restaurant manager, and BOH is stable but sushi holidays in November need considering.

Weekly hygiene compliance could not be retrieved because of wider Mapal issues at 12pm on 12/10 and will be updated when it is back online; pest control, fire, electrical, gas and ventilation compliance are complete.
High priority maintenance: the Maki Biru beer line does not work at all, an emergency light is out on the ramen light, and the bar fridge handle has come off and has only been superglued.

Other maintenance: wobbly tables keep coming undone after fixing, the heat lamps, the Kobas printer, a stock room that is too hot, an intermittently leaking bar fridge, waiter stations 1 and 2 coming away from the wall and the light above the donburi.

Broken wall tiles behind the grease trap need a follow up with Kris, and the floor around the old grip taped areas has missing panels causing trip hazards and grime build up, which should be fixable in house outside service hours.
Deliveroo food quality, correct orders and the resulting reviews remain the area for improvement, though Deliveroo reviews look better this week, and the Slerp instant ready issue has been addressed.

The university frozen ramen promotion is postponed while the site awaits correct date labels from head office, and lunch, XOXO, Deliveroo, Slerp and Deliveroo vouchers and the book launch are upcoming.
The shopping centre has reached out about a Halloween menu and events.

Region: five of the nine Scotland and Newcastle sites ran food cost above 25% (Maki 12, 1, 7, 3 and 8), which the Scotland BOH meeting of 13/10 linked to loyalty programme and delivery platform discounts across the group.

Region: new tonkotsu and chicken broth arrives from 15/10 and needs no added water; defrost it a day ahead and reheat it in a pot rather than straight on the heat, and a digital Brix meter is arriving to replace checking by eye, though not every site has one yet (Scotland BOH meeting 13/10).

Region: new chicken arrives on 15/10 and the new char siu (different shape) and pre cooked frozen beef from 19/10, starting at Maki 8; defrost the beef a day ahead and grill or pan fry it for 15 seconds a side before slicing, holding extra stock because it cannot be used on the day it arrives (Scotland BOH meeting 13/10).

Region: the frozen ramen promotion is postponed by one week, and Penny is checking with Michael whether frozen ramen counts in food cost or separately, as some sites have already bought it (Scotland BOH meeting 13/10).
Gross delivery sales were close to £8,000 (AM Updates 14/10).
Ka Ho has fed the 3 star bill splitting review back to Joe (AM Updates 14/10).

Region: Ka Ho put food cost of 25.3% to 27.2% at Maki 1, Fountainbridge, M7, M8 and M12 down to promotions lifting usage while sales projections were not adjusted; Michael said site leaders can ask for food cost and wage budget increases (AM Updates 14/10).
Region: a level 8 Halloween ramen with a super spicy factory chilli paste is launching with a video; one bag per site, about a teaspoon per bowl (AM Updates 14/10).
Region: snooze out of stock items on both Deliverect and the POS, or the whole delivery order fails (AM Updates 14/10).
Region: wage revenue baseline is 21% with up to 2% leeway; drinks cost moves to management, food cost to head chefs, new OKRs due end of November (AM Updates 14/10).
